{"id": "9244bde6-368f-4f33-9f3f-2225aef7b193", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_scUNXZaBxEFa9mRW8Z1hKI", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Scaling and throughput best practices\",\"context\":\"## `bedrock-mantle` endpoint: throughput and quotas\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle` endpoint has the following quota behavior:\\n\\n* Models with published quotas have separate per-model, per-Region input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas.\\n* The endpoint does not enforce RPM quotas. Two workloads with the same RPM can consume very different amounts of capacity, so plan and rate-limit by tokens and concurrency instead of RPM alone.\\n* When a request is admitted, the input-token check includes the input tokens plus the requested `max_tokens` value. After the response completes, the unused part of that reservation is replenished. Set `max_tokens` no higher than your application needs.\\n* Models without published TPM quotas do not currently have per-account TPM quotas exposed in Service Quotas. This does not mean that throughput is unlimited; internal service capacity and transient rate limiting still apply.\\n* Batch inference and Provisioned Throughput are available only through `bedrock-runtime`. Service-tier and model support varies by model.\\n\\nDefault values and your account's allocations can vary by model, Region, and usage history. For current values, quota evaluation details, and the AWS Support process for requesting an increase, see Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint. See the applicable Models at a glance for model-specific endpoint, service-tier, and feature support\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Quotas for Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"# Quotas for Amazon Bedrock\\n\\nYour AWS account has default quotas, formerly referred to as limits, for Amazon Bedrock. To view\\nservice quotas for Amazon Bedrock, do one of the following:\\n\\n* Follow the steps at Viewing service\\n quotas and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service.\\n* Refer to the Amazon Bedrock service quotas in the AWS General Reference.\\n\\nModel inference in Amazon Bedrock is controlled by quotas on token usage. Some models use tokens at a higher rate. For more information about these rates and how to optimize your token usage, see How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock.\\n\\nEmbedding models are an exception: they are throttled by requests per minute (RPM) rather than tokens per minute (TPM). Use the RPM quota when you plan capacity or request a quota increase for an embedding model. For more information, see Amazon Titan Text Embeddings models.\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock offers two inference endpoints \u2013 `bedrock-runtime` and `bedrock-mantle` \u2013 each with its own per-model quota allocations. Traffic to the two endpoints is tracked against separate quotas, even when calling the same underlying model. For details, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint and Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint.\\n\\nTo maintain the performance of the service and to ensure appropriate usage of Amazon Bedrock, the\\ndefault quotas assigned to an account might be updated depending on regional factors,\\naccount age, usage history, payment history, fraudulent usage, and/or approval of a quota increase request.\\nAs a result, the quotas that apply to your account might be lower than the default values\\nlisted in the Amazon Bedrock service quotas. To check the values that apply to your account, use Service Quotas as\\ndescribed earlier in this topic.\\n\\nQuota increases aren't granted automatically. For the request process and the conditions\\nthat apply to a request, see Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock\\n* Monitor your token usage by counting tokens before running inference\\n* Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\\n* Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\\n* Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Quota management\\n\\nCross-Region inference quotas on the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint are measured in tokens per minute (TPM) per model. Each quota combines input and output tokens against a single limit. US geographic and global inference profiles have separate quota allocations, so switching between them changes the pool you draw from.\\n\\nToken consumption combines input tokens, cache-write input tokens, and output tokens. Output tokens are multiplied by the model\u2019s burndown rate, so output-heavy workloads consume quota faster than raw token counts suggest. Before a production rollout, request quota increases early and monitor quota utilization. Test with representative prompts, output lengths, streaming behavior, concurrency, and peak traffic.\\n\\nTo request a quota increase, follow these steps:\\n\\n1. Open the Service Quotas console in `ca-central-1` or `ca-west-1`.\\n2. Choose **Amazon Bedrock**, then select the quota named \u201cCross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute\u201d for the model that you need.\\n3. Choose **Request increase at account level**, enter your target value, and submit the request.\\n\\nFor details on how token usage and costs are tracked, see Track usage and costs in Amazon Bedrock\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/access-openai-gpt-models-on-amazon-bedrock-from-canada-with-cross-region-inference/\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Analyze Amazon Bedrock cost spikes with AWS DevOps Agent\",\"context\":\"## Introduction\\n\\nOrganizations that run generative AI workloads on [Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-bedrock.html) pay by the token. Unlike traditional compute resources where costs scale predictably with instance hours, with Amazon Bedrock one misconfigured application can use millions of tokens in minutes. Retry loops that don't back off, prompts that pass entire documents without truncation, and batch jobs without concurrency controls sometimes generate significant unexpected charges.\\n\\nThe challenge is timing. [AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html) updates hours after consumption occurs. By the time a cost anomaly appears in billing dashboards, the damage is done.\\n\\nHowever, Amazon Bedrock publishes **InputTokenCount** and **OutputTokenCount** metrics to [CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/WhatIsCloudWatch.html) within minutes of every model invocation. These metrics represent the earliest available cost signal in your environment. For more information about token counts, see [How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html).\\n\\nFor organizations that work with [AWS Enterprise Support](https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/plans/enterprise/), the Technical Account Manager (TAM) can help you design monitoring strategies that catch these anomalies early. AWS Cloud Support Engineers regularly assist customers to configure CloudWatch alarms and automate investigation workflows for their generative AI workloads.\\n\\nThis article outlines how to turn CloudWatch token metrics into an automated detection and investigation pipeline that moves from token spike to autonomous root cause analysis in minutes. The solution uses the following AWS services:\\n\\n- [CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html)\\n\\n- [Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)\\n\\n- [AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html)\\n\\n- [AWS DevOps Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/devopsagent/latest/userguide/what-is-devops-agent.html)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/AR_gbMkpbaTJOwRyCpqGf6uA/analyze-amazon-bedrock-cost-spikes-with-aws-devops-agent\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search docs for Bedrock mantle endpoint quotas and billing"}

Supported providers include DeepSeek, Google, MiniMax, Mistral, Moonshot AI, Nvidia, and OpenAI. Project Mantle simplifies model onboarding, provides performant and reliable serverless inference, offers sophisticated quality of service controls, and delivers OpenAI API compatibility out-of-the-box. {"id": "2cd51211-d3ff-4e47-98f3-66af23f859b8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes. The `-mantle-` in that usage type means your Claude Sonnet 5 traffic is billed as `bedrock-mantle` traffic, so the `[bedrock-mantle endpoint]` quotas apply to it.

**Why that holds**
- The CUR usage-type documentation lists the format `{region}-{model}-mantle-{token-type}-standard` for `bedrock-mantle` requests. Your line `USE1-anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard` matches it.
- `bedrock-runtime` standard-tier usage types have no `mantle` segment. An example is `USE1-Claude4.6Sonnet-input-tokens`.
- Bedrock tracks the two endpoints against separate per-model quota allocations, even for the same underlying model. Your `bedrock-runtime` quotas wouldn't apply to this traffic.

**How the mantle quota works**
- Input and output tokens per minute are separate quotas for each model in each Region. In your case that means Sonnet 5 in `us-east-1`.
- A request is checked against the input quota using its input tokens plus its `max_tokens` value. If `max_tokens` isn't set, the model's maximum is used. Unused reservation is returned to the quota after the response completes.
- A request that would exceed the quota gets an HTTP 429.
- There is no requests-per-minute quota on this endpoint.
- Some models have no TPM quota published in Service Quotas. That doesn't mean throughput is unlimited, because internal capacity limits and transient throttling still apply.

**Things to check**
- The Anthropic Messages API is available on both endpoints. A `-mantle-` line therefore means someone is calling `https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/anthropic/v1/messages`. This is common when callers use Bedrock API keys or Workspaces. If you expected `bedrock-runtime`, look for clients using that base URL.
- If any traffic also goes through `bedrock-runtime`, you'd see separate Cost Explorer lines without `mantle` in the name. Those use the runtime quotas, and you should size each endpoint independently.
- Quota values vary by account, Region and usage history. Check the actual value in Service Quotas for Amazon Bedrock in `us-east-1`.

If you're seeing 429s on this traffic, I can look at your account's quota values and the `bedrock-mantle` CloudWatch token metrics. I'd need to know which Region and time window to look at.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
